stem: Mark-up is gross profit expressed as a percentage of …

options.rationale: Correct: mark-up is calculated on cost.

explanation: Mark-up = gross profit ÷ cost × 100; margin = gross profit ÷ selling price × 100.

stem: A trader uses a mark-up of 25%. What is her gross profit margin?

options.rationale: Margin and mark-up are not equal; they have different bases.
This converts the wrong way (25 ÷ 75).
This is 100 minus the mark-up, which has no meaning here.

explanation: Cost 100, gross profit 25, selling price 125: margin = 25/125 = 20%.

stem: A shop's gross profit margin is 40%. What is its mark-up (to one decimal place)?

options.rationale: This converts the wrong way (40 ÷ 140).
Mark-up is always larger than margin.
This is cost as a percentage of selling price.

explanation: Selling price 100, gross profit 40, cost 60: mark-up = 40/60 = 66.7%.

stem: Cost of sales was US\$27,600 and goods are sold at a mark-up of 30%. What was the revenue?

This is the gross profit.

stem: Revenue US\$52,500; mark-up 50%; opening inventory US\$6,100; purchases US\$36,400. What was the closing inventory?

stem: Which statement about mark-up and margin is **true** for a business that makes a gross profit?

options.content: The margin is always greater than the mark-up
options.rationale: Revenue is the larger base, so the margin is smaller.

options.content: They are equal when sales are high
options.rationale: They are never equal while there is a gross profit.

options.content: The margin can be more than 100%
options.rationale: Gross profit cannot exceed revenue.

options.content: The mark-up is always greater than the margin
options.rationale: Correct: the same gross profit is divided by a smaller base.

explanation: Cost of sales is less than revenue, so gross profit ÷ cost is larger than gross profit ÷ revenue.
hints: Which is bigger: cost or selling price?

stem: A hardware shop sells a wheelbarrow for US\$84 at a mark-up of 40%. What did the wheelbarrow cost the shop?

options.rationale: This deducts 40% of the selling price, treating 40% as a margin.
Cost cannot exceed the selling price when there is a profit.
This is 40% of the selling price.

stem: A mark-up of 100% is the same as a gross profit margin of 50%.
explanation: True. Cost 100, gross profit 100, selling price 200: 100/200 = 50%.

stem: If cost of sales is US\$40,000 and the margin is 20%, the gross profit is US\$8,000.
explanation: False. A margin is a percentage of selling price. Revenue = 40,000 × 100/80 = 50,000, so gross profit = 10,000. US\$8,000 is 20% of cost.

explanation: Cost structure: cost 100, gross profit 20, selling price 120. Gross profit = 91,200 × 20/120 = 15,200. Taking 20% of revenue gives 18,240, the margin/mark-up swap.

stem: Tatenda's opening inventory was US\$7,240, purchases US\$58,960 and closing inventory US\$8,200. His gross profit margin is 25%. Calculate his revenue, to the nearest cent.
explanation: Cost of sales = 7,240 + 58,960 − 8,200 = 58,000. Revenue = 58,000 × 100/75 = 77,333.33. Adding 25% to cost gives 72,500, which uses the margin as a mark-up.
workedSolution: 1. Cost of sales = 7,240 + 58,960 − 8,200 = 58,000. Revenue = 58,000 × 100/75 = 77,333.33. Adding 25% to cost gives 72,500, which uses the margin as a mark-up.
hints: With a 25% margin, cost of sales is 75% of revenue.

stem: Explain why a mark-up of 25% does not give a gross profit margin of 25%.

points.description: Mark-up is measured on cost; margin on selling price
Selling price is larger than cost (125 v 100), so the same gross profit is a smaller percentage of it (20%)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The mark-up compares the gross profit with cost, but the margin compares it with the selling price. With cost 100 and gross profit 25, selling price is 125, so the margin is 25/125 = 20%.

stem: Rudo wants a gross profit margin of 40% on a dress that costs her US\$45. She plans to sell it for US\$63. Advise her whether this price meets her target, showing your working.

points.description: Price of US\$63 gives a margin of 18/63 = 28.6% (she has added 40% to cost)
Advice: raise the price to US\$75, or accept a lower margin

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: For a 40% margin, cost must be 60% of price: 45 ÷ 0.6 = US\$75. At US\$63 her gross profit is US\$18, a margin of only 28.6%, because she has added 40% to cost instead. She should charge US\$75 to meet her target.

explanation: She has confused a 40% mark-up with a 40% margin.
hints: With a 40% margin, cost is 60% of the selling price.

stem: A fire at Farai Gumbo's hardware shop in Kadoma on 31 December 2025 destroyed part of his inventory. He sells all goods at a mark-up of 25%. For 2025: revenue US\$61,500; inventory at 1 January 2025 US\$5,860; purchases US\$47,250. Inventory that survived the fire cost US\$2,450.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State Farai's gross profit margin, to one decimal place.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the cost of sales for 2025.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the inventory that Farai should have held at 31 December 2025.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the cost of the inventory destroyed by the fire.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Explain why the mark-up method gives only an estimate of the inventory destroyed.

points.description: It assumes every item was sold at exactly the same mark-up
Discounts, price changes, damaged goods or theft during the year would change the real cost of sales

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The calculation assumes all goods were sold at a 25% mark-up. If some were sold at a discount, or goods were stolen or damaged earlier in the year, the true cost of sales and so the true loss would be different.

parts.explanation: The figure is only as good as the assumption of a constant mark-up.

explanation:
Workings:

| Trading figures | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Opening inventory | 5,860 |
| Add: Purchases | 47,250 |
| Goods available for sale | 53,110 |
| Less: Closing inventory (should be held) | (3,910) |
| Cost of sales | 49,200 |
| Gross profit | 12,300 |
| Revenue | 61,500 |

Inventory destroyed: 3,910 − 2,450 = 1,460.
hints: Cost structure: cost 100, gross profit 25, selling price 125.
